# url_fetch Usage Guide

<!-- socrates:section id="purpose" kind="purpose" tags="tools" -->
## Purpose

- `url_fetch`: Fetch one exact http(s) URL as bounded text or metadata. Use this to read a specific page, docs URL, redirect, JSON, CSV, or plain-text resource. It does not search the web, crawl links, save files, install packages, or return binary bodies. For broad web search use configured search/MCP capabilities; for complex parsing or comparison, combine this with read/search and Terminal one-off scripts.
<!-- /socrates:section -->

<!-- socrates:section id="when_to_use" kind="routing" tags="tools" -->
## When To Use

- Use `url_fetch` when the active task requires its cataloged read/retrieval capability.
<!-- /socrates:section -->

<!-- socrates:section id="inputs" kind="schema" tags="tools" -->
## Inputs

- `url_fetch` uses the one canonical schema owned by `tool.url_fetch`; send only documented fields and do not add aliases or placeholder values.
<!-- /socrates:section -->

<!-- socrates:section id="workflow" kind="workflow" tags="tools" -->
## Workflow

1. Select `url_fetch` only for the behavior described above, pass an exact valid input, and use its persisted result as evidence before continuing.
<!-- /socrates:section -->

<!-- socrates:section id="failure_handling" kind="recovery" tags="tools" -->

- If input validation fails, correct the call against the canonical schema; do not guess, normalize, or silently drop fields.
- If execution returns a typed error, preserve it as evidence and either correct the call or explain the blocker.
